transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I am only here because... well, it’s a whole mess, to be honest with you. See, my husband’s sister, she has been working this family business from the inside. And I mean really working it. I’ve been sitting back, just watching it happen, because I don't go out to a job myself, so I have the time to see what people are really up to when they think nobody is paying attention. She’s been doing all these little things, making these side comments and rearranging things just so she can get total control of the money. 

And it is not just the money, it is about pushing me entirely out of the decisions. I used to have a say in what we did, but now she has got her hands in absolutely everything. And my husband and all the other folks in the family, they just try to smooth it over. They tell me she is just trying to help out, or that I am looking too hard at it, but I know what I know. I have eyes. I know exactly what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

It started way back, and ever since then it has just been this slow, sneaky process of pushing me right out the picture. You do not just accidentally take over someone's financial life. So that is why I came in, because nobody else will listen to the truth of what is going on right under their noses, and it is just exhausting trying to explain it to people who refuse to see it.
Do you believe that your husband’s sister is intentionally trying to harm or manipulate you in some way?

Intentionally? Oh, absolutely. There is no... there's no 'accidental' about it. You don't just accidentally start taking over the books and making decisions without asking the person who’s been married to your brother for twenty-some years. It is pure manipulation, doctor. Like I was trying to explain, that is exactly why I came in here to talk to somebody, because my husband’s sister has been working this family business from the inside out just so she can get total control of the money. 

And it’s to push me out of the decisions, plain and simple. Just last month—well, maybe it was the end of October, right around Halloween because I remember I was buying candy at the drugstore when I figured it out—she calls up our main supplier and changes the delivery schedule without even running it by me. Used to be, we’d sit down at the kitchen table and go over all the receipts together, but now? Now she acts like I don't even know how to add two and two because I didn't finish high school. She uses all these big words and spreadsheets just to confuse the issue, but I see right through it. 

And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—my husband especially, he’ll say, 'Oh, she’s just taking a load off your shoulders, honey, she went to community college for this'—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. You can't tell me I'm not seeing it. It’s like a chess game to her. She moves a piece here, a piece there, making these little comments about how I shouldn't worry my head about the taxes, and suddenly I'm completely boxed out of my own life. And it hurts, you know? It really hurts that nobody else sees the malice in it. They just smile and nod and let her take the reins, while I'm standing right there watching her steal my place. I mean, if you saw someone doing that in your own home, wouldn't you call it intentional? Because I sure do, and I am just sick and tired of being treated like I'm the crazy one for noticing it.
Do you ever feel like people are plotting against you or working together in ways that they aren't admitting to, even when others tell you that's not the case?

Well, that is exactly what I've been trying to tell you since I sat down! It’s like... well, like I said, I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business specifically so she can get control of the money and push me completely out of the decisions. And when you ask if they're working together... yes! They might not be having secret meetings in the basement, but they are absolutely all going along with it. 

No matter how folks try to smooth it over, they are all letting it happen. My husband, his brother, they all just stand by. I'll bring it up, I'll say, 'Look at what she did with the accounts this week,' and they just give each other that look. You know that look? Like I'm a child throwing a tantrum. They tell me I'm imagining things, that she's just 'updating the system' or whatever excuse they've all agreed on for the week. But they know. They have to know. They just won't admit that they've all silently decided I don't matter anymore just because I don't have some fancy high school diploma. 

But I am not blind, doctor. I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. I watch how they talk around me, how they change the subject when I walk into the kitchen, how my husband just rubs the back of his neck and sighs instead of defending me. It’s all connected. They are all letting her do this to me, and it is just exhausting that they won't just look me in the eye and admit what they are doing.

This is consistent with Delusional Disorder, specifically the jealous or persecutory type, which is coded as F22.0. Other candidates related to mood disorders (e.g., F32.x, F33.x) and adjustment disorders (e.g., F43.2x) are less consistent with the presentation, as there is little evidence of prominent depressive symptoms, mood disturbance, or typical adjustment stressors. No evidence of recurrent brief depressive episodes or persistent complex bereavement reaction remains compelling.
